title: Mandate Wallet — actual local EVM and App demo

stages.caption: Actual App + local EVM. Mock USDC; trusted fixture owner. External browser-wallet approval is not demonstrated.
stages.narration: This is the actual Mandate App connected to a temporary local EVM. All funds are mock USDC. A trusted test fixture has created the mandate and session. This recording does not demonstrate an external browser wallet.

stages.caption: Owner-approved scope: 0.15 USDC shared budget, 0.10 maximum payment, fixed recipients and requests.
stages.narration: The mandate specifies the owner, session signer and approved recipient. The root budget is fifteen cents, and the single-payment maximum is ten cents. The agent credential does not create these permissions. Gas is separate from the USDC budget.

stages.caption: Fetch actual x402 terms for the approved ETH request before registration.
stages.narration: The services page contains approved request scope. We fetch the merchant's actual x four oh two quote for ETH statistics. The price is one cent. Discovery metadata cannot expand the approved recipient or request.

stages.caption: The real token transfer succeeded; the controlled merchant returned HTTP 500. Result remains unchecked.
stages.narration: The first call registers the payment, reserves budget and settles the token transfer. The controlled merchant then returns HTTP five hundred. The App correctly shows payment paid, service failed, and result unchecked. A successful payment does not mean successful delivery.

stages.caption: Recover the same order. Settlement hash and nonce stay unchanged; no second payment.
stages.narration: Recovery uses the original order and payment identity. The service now returns data and the result checker accepts it. The settlement hash remains unchanged. The wallet has paid one cent, with fourteen cents of authorization left. This retry does not create another payment.

stages.caption: Separate-process verification: financial checks pass; overall remains incomplete for missing HTTPS/history guarantees.
stages.narration: We disclose the request and result and run the separate evidence verifier. Financial and record checks pass. The overall status remains incomplete because the paid merchant has no independent HTTPS witness and unseen history is not proven complete. Hidden content would remain unchecked.

stages.caption: Unsigned revocation preview. Confirmation stays disabled without an external owner wallet.
stages.narration: The App prepares an unsigned request to revoke this session. The confirmation button remains disabled because no external owner wallet is connected. We will apply this exact request using the trusted local fixture. This is test-owner execution, not a claim of real browser-wallet acceptance.

stages.caption: The trusted fixture owner signs the exact request on the local chain; App reconciliation confirms it applied.
stages.narration: The trusted fixture owner now submits the exact revocation transaction to the local chain. Reconciliation confirms that the request applied and the session is revoked. The earlier paid commitment remains occupied; revocation does not refund a completed purchase.

stages.caption: A second approved service cannot spend through the revoked session. Token balance and payment count stay unchanged.
stages.narration: We try the BTC step through the revoked session. The client refuses it, and the payment count remains one. The first purchase stays paid and valid. A new agent instruction cannot revive the revoked grant or expand its authority.

stages.caption: Actual local fixture recording. Independent audit and complete external-wallet/mobile owner acceptance remain open.
stages.narration: The security view states the boundaries. Session keys may be exposed to the host, but the contract still restricts financial scope. Same-host evidence and controllers do not isolate an administrator. Public testnet transaction evidence is provided separately. Independent security review and full external-wallet and mobile acceptance remain open.
